questions.q: What is SAQL used for in CRM Analytics?
options: Writing Apex triggers on Salesforce objects
Querying data in CRM Analytics datasets, behind lenses and dashboards
questions.explain: SAQL is the query language CRM Analytics uses behind lenses, dashboard steps, and the explorer to read from datasets.

questions.q: In a SAQL query, what does each statement take and produce?
options: An input stream and an output stream
A user and a permission set
questions.explain: Each statement reads an input stream, applies an operation, and writes an output stream that the next statement can use.

questions.q: Which statement decides which columns, including aggregates like sum() or count(), appear in the output after a group?
questions.explain: group only sets up the grouping. foreach ... generate defines the output columns and aggregates.

questions.q: Which line follows SAQL quoting rules?
options: q = filter q by StageName == Closed Won
questions.explain: Field names take single quotes, text values take double quotes, and the statement ends with a semicolon.

questions.q: What is a good way to start learning SAQL, according to the lesson?
options: Memorize the full function reference first
Avoid the SAQL editor until you are an expert
Write raw SAQL only, never using the chart builder
Build a chart with clicks, then switch to the SAQL editor and read the generated query
questions.explain: Switching a lens to SAQL mode shows the exact query the platform generated, which is an easy way to see how clicks map to statements.
